title: Texts chosen for more than readability
statement: Choose a course's texts for their purpose, the knowledge they build in sequence, a balance of genres and their quality, judged by reading them, not by a readability score alone.
example: One course chosen mainly by readability had essentially no poetry and no drama, short of its own roughly 40/40/20 target.
detail: A course review found a Grade 3 course's texts chosen mainly by Lexile: overwhelmingly informational, with essentially no poetry and no drama, short of the course's own roughly 40/40/20 literary, informational and vocabulary target; Lexile alone, it noted, mishandles poetry and narrative and cannot tell whether a text is worth reading (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/feedback_clean.md`). It asked for texts chosen for a coherent knowledge sequence and a genre balance, with complexity judged qualitatively as well as by Lexile. The reading team's insights BrainLift holds that text difficulty is a match among text, reader knowledge and task that no single readability number can gate (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0121-teaching-comprehension-insights-brainlift.qmd`).
against: Another review notes that the 40% target was itself admitted as an assumption with an open source ask (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/redteam-sources/g5-reading-redteam-round1-2026-07-06.md`).

evidence.quote: Lexile alone also mishandles poetry and narrative and cannot tell you whether a text is worth reading.
